program: Whole recipient; conditional crisis hotline health and signed net household resources

acceptance.evidence: docs/geography-discovery/nyc-samaritans-independent-20261005.md; independent original-source and twenty-case/181-check arithmetic challenge accepted.

what: Samaritans of New York offers free, anonymous, confidential, round-the-clock emotional support and suicide prevention.
The recipient also offers bereavement support and public education, whose separate effects are not monetized here.
We examine incremental crisis episodes supported by an ordinary gift against existing free NYC988 and other support, with signed household-resource effects.
strengths: Current operator pages identify a specific active hotline and its consent and privacy policies.
Original fiscal returns reconcile annual recipient costs, including separately netted event expense in FY2022.
The model distinguishes calls from episodes and values common-alive distress and net cash effects without adding survivor earnings.
reservations: Unique callers, causal death prevention, persistent utility change and extra gift-funded capacity are not observed.
Free NYC988 is a substantive alternative; hotline studies do not measure this recipient’s next-dollar effect.
The conditional central is about $30.7M per better life, with slightly negative net resources; null, adverse and funding-replacement cases are explicit.

sections.what: The recipient is Samaritans of New York Inc., EIN 13-3164464. Its [current crisis page](https://samaritansnyc.org/crisis/) describes free 24/7 anonymous confidential listening, no caller tracing unless location is shared and no police/EMS action without caller consent. Ordinary telephone-provider charges may still apply. Its [overview](https://samaritansnyc.org/get-support/) also offers bereavement and education. An unrestricted gift does not create a verified restricted hotline slot. The model conservatively charges the whole recipient’s cost while counting only conditional crisis effects; other portfolio effects remain unknown rather than zero.
sections.monitoring: The latest original return reports FY 2024-labeled 37,734 contacts, including 29,129 crisis calls. They are not unique callers or resolved independent episodes. The overview’s 50,000 contacts/30,000 volunteerhours and older 2023 education/bereavement totals have different reporting scope and dates and are not a matched current denominator. Anonymous service limits residence and unique-person measurement. Needed data include privacy-preserving repeat-episode counts, wait/abandon rates, unmet demand, follow-up retention, actual clinical outcomes, local residence, covered staffing and a dated next-dollar capacity plan. No source supplies these measurements.
sections.qualitative:
[Gould 2007](https://doi.org/10.1521/suli.2007.37.3.338) followed 1,085 suicidal callers at eight US centers; 380 (35%) completed follow-up. Distress and suicidality fell, but there was no untreated control, substantial follow-up attrition and no generic utility or causal mortality estimate. The [original randomized ASIST training study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3838495/) compares trained versus existing counselors, not a hotline versus no help; its primary indexed abstract supports immediate distress outcomes, not deaths averted. Full text was inaccessible in this pass, so no numerical effect is imported. The [2026 national 988 study](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/article-abstract/2848066) compares observed 15–34-year-old mortality with a forecast after the national launch, not an isolated Samaritans donation. Its 11% national association cannot identify this program’s effect. [Current NYC 988](https://nyc988.cityofnewyork.us/en/) offers free 24/7 calls/text/chat, languages, referrals and follow-up. Noncoercive anonymous listening may reach people avoiding other routes; it may also delay escalation for some crises. Consent policy is not proof that net harms are absent. Independent delay/safety harm is modeled, with adverse/null cases.

The primary Gould full text also excludes 654 callers considered too acutely suicidal to administer the assessment, adding selection bias to follow-up attrition. The assumed episode multiplier is an approximate repeat-contact adjustment, not a verified distinct-person registry; repeated crises within one person remain a source of uncertainty. Mortality probabilities are deliberately small, but this does not establish real unique lives saved.
sections.cost:
Our conditional combined estimate is **$30.7 million per better life**: ten health-and-household-resource-equivalent years in the NYC metro area. The initial health-only estimate was $13.9 million. The change reflects revised crisis-episode, clinical and household-resource assumptions, not an observed deterioration in the hotline.

**What additional funding could provide.** The latest annual expense is $1.29 million. Historical crisis-call volume, a judged current-scale transfer and a 40% funding response imply about 72 additional call equivalents per $10,000 mathematical normalization, or roughly $138 per additional call equivalent. Assuming five contacts per independent crisis gives about 14.5 crisis episodes, or $691 per episode. These are conditional average-support calculations, not verified additional staffing prices or unique callers. The full recipient's administration, fundraising, education and support costs are charged once; donated volunteer hours are not automatically monetized or added twice.

**Health.** Existing free NYC988 and other help remain in the counterfactual. The model assumes a modest acute mortality-risk difference among a judged high-risk subgroup, one-day response delay and a finite twenty-year survival tail. Short-lived distress improvement applies only to people alive in both worlds. A separate safety/delay burden remains in clinical-null cases. Hotline studies support the plausibility of immediate relief, not these numerical mortality or generic-utility assumptions. Repeat contacts and unique crisis episodes are uncertain.

**Net household resources.** Small one-off phone charges and uncovered care or transport costs are subtracted after free calling, insurance and other support. A small response group avoids actual lost disposable pay, net of taxes, benefits, paid leave and work costs. Caller time, gross wages, ordinary earnings of newly surviving participants and retail value of free services receive no cash credit. Nested care/no-care groups use a shared resource ledger rather than duplicate receipts.

The [Coefficient Giving-inspired logarithmic comparison](https://coefficientgiving.org/research/cost-effectiveness/) uses a judged $25,000 annual household-resource baseline. Common-alive survival, dated receipt, local attribution and discounting apply once. Half of positive income-equivalent welfare is retained to reduce overlap with distress relief; negative resource costs are charged fully. These are unmeasured resource priors, not caller financial outcomes.

At the $10,000 mathematical normalization—not a gift recommendation—the central case yields about 0.00331 health years and −0.000057 income-equivalent years, or 0.00325 combined years. Scaling funding and activity together does not change the price. The twenty scenarios include weaker and stronger clinical responses, repeated contacts, delay, low acute risk, shorter survival, signed pay losses, overlap, zero expansion, full clinical substitution and adverse outcomes. An external-resource companion adds $100 per episode for selected unrecognized volunteer or public resources, not a complete societal-cost inventory. Other portfolio benefits, unique-person outcomes and actual gift-sensitive capacity remain unmeasured.
sections.funding:
Original FY 2025, FY 2024 and FY 2022 returns were freshly retrieved; FY 2023 was not available in the inspected original index, so these are not a consecutive three-year series. FY 2025 audited expense $1,288,400 differs by $1 from Part IX $1,288,399 (program 926,923/management 183,353/fundraising 178,123); direct event expense is blank and is not added. FY 2024 Part IX/audit $1,194,820; FY 2022 Part IX $902,572 plus separately netted direct event $77,785 reconciles to audited gross $980,357. FY 2025 prior-year expense comparator $1,115,933 differs from the FY 2024 original $1,194,820; no comparable mean is forced.

Latest government grants $375,396, revenue $1,002,201, deficit $286,198 and prior-period adjustment−$5,081 accompany ending net assets without restriction $439,448. Cash $283,011, grants receivable $107,596 and accounts receivable $79,916 mean net assets are not cash runway. FY 2024 government grants $370,000 and FY 2022$439,297 are not evidence of uncovered current capacity. Grant renewals, fund restrictions, staffing vacancies, unmet calls and donation replacement remain unknown. No audit opinion/control report was inspected and no donation/contact was made.

model.costScope: Donor marginal capacity scenario from full annual average expense; unknown external volunteer/public resources not known zero.
model.geographicAttribution: g=.8 anonymous-caller MSA residence judgment; applied once to health and each income path.
model.formula: k=ln(1+r); F(q,t)=(1-exp(-q*t))/q; E=G*b*N*f*episode/C; B=E*a; survival gain=B*s*R*e*exp(-(m+k)*L)*u*F(m+k,T); common-alive morbidity=B*(1-sR)*p*v*exp(-(m+k)*L)*F(m+k,days/365); harm=E*h*exp(-(m+k)*L); H=mortality+morbidity-harm. Income=.5*people*ln(1+gain/sequentialBaseline)*commonAlive(receipt)*g*independence/(1+r)^receipt; price10=10*(G+E*external)/(g*H+income), null if denominator<=0.
model.counterfactual: Free NYC988, other support, grants, covered care and paid leave continue. b controls incremental scale; a clinical advantage; resource incidence is separately net causal differential.
model.attribution: Calls are not unique people. Independent episode/household judgments prevent literal contact multiplication. Common-alive utility/resources exclude acute baseline deaths and additional-survivor earnings. Negatives full credit; sequential bases avoid log ledger inconsistency.
model.uncertainty: Unweighted scenarios, not credible intervals or measured causal next-dollar effects. Outcome/funding/economic priors are judgments; missing other-program effects remain unknown.
model.nativeCosts: Latest whole-recipient audited expense1288400; mathematical gift10000, no arbitrary donor-specific framing; selected external-cost companion only.

historicalAlphaModel.costScope: Full recipient annual audited-recognized expense incl training/bereavement/admin; volunteer opportunity cost separate. Current cost and FY2024-labeled calls are a forecasting proxy.
historicalAlphaModel.geographicAttribution: OMB23-01 22-county MSA. g=.8 subjective local share; anonymous hotline residence cannot be inferred from NYC area code.
historicalAlphaModel.formula: E=N*z*l; B=E*r*a*b; D=sum(t=1..L)u*exp(-m*t)/(1+d)^t; Qall=B*(s*R*e*D+(1-s*R*e)*w*v*days/365/(1+d)^(days/365))-h; Qlocal=g*Qall; cost=C+volunteerCost; price10=10*cost/Qlocal if positive.
historicalAlphaModel.counterfactual: 988, clinical/family care, other regional hotlines and ordinary recovery continue; r discounts equivalent alternative assistance, a discounts other contributors, b discounts replacement financing.
historicalAlphaModel.attribution: l=1 preserves hotline output per historical whole-recipient dollar, not a restricted gift. Distinct episodes z=.2; fatal-risk subgroup s=.25; no extra benefit for repeated contacts, trainings or other affiliates.
historicalAlphaModel.uncertainty: Very weak conditional health estimate. Neither short-term fatal risk nor call-induced risk reduction is locally measured; the favorable national evidence does not calibrate them. Financial period and narrative output year are not assumed identical. Caller residence is unmeasured: g=.8 is a scenario assumption, not an observed NYC-MSA share.
historicalAlphaModel.nativeOutcomes: Crisis calls -> deduplicated episodes -> acute distress relief and small near-term fatal-risk reduction.
historicalAlphaModel.nativeCosts: 29,129/1,288,400=0.02261 crisis calls per dollar; after assumed five calls/episode0.00452 episodes per dollar. Not observed marginal purchased capacity.
